newsitem.title: CHINA: Foreign banks to do renminbi business in Shenzhen.
newsitem.headline: Foreign banks to do renminbi business in Shenzhen.

text.p: China's central bank governor Dai Xianglong has said foreign banks in Shenzhen will be allowed to conduct domestic yuan currency business in the near future, Shenzhen Communist Party Secretary Li Youwei said on Thursday.

"Dai Xianglong... clearly pointed out during a recent fact-finding visit to Shenzhen that foreign-funded banks in Shenzhen will be allowed to gradually engage in renminbi business in the not too-distant future," Li told a news conference in the booming city that borders Hong Kong.
He gave no timetable for when foreign banks in Shenzhen would be allowed to start yuan, or renminbi, business.

China has so far given permission to nine foreign banks to conduct limited yuan currency business in China, and all have been required to set up their main branches in Shanghai's Pudong district before starting local currency transactions.
There are 52 foreign-funded banks in Shenzhen, the second largest contingent after Shanghai, Li said but gave no more details.
